name: Build Max Heap
description: Builds a max-heap from an unsorted array in O(n) time using the bottom-up heapification approach. Root is always the maximum element.
aim: Rearrange array into a max-heap where every parent node is greater than or equal to its children, enabling O(log n) extract-max operations.
howItWorks: Start from last non-leaf node: index n/2-1
Apply heapify-down for each node from n/2-1 down to 0
Heapify-down: compare node with children, swap with largest child if smaller
Recursively heapify down the swapped subtree
After all nodes processed, array satisfies max-heap property

time.bestCase: Build heap is O(n) — tight analysis, not O(n log n)
time.worstCase: O(n) for any input — not O(n log n) as might be expected

complexity.spaceDescription: In-place — no extra array needed, just recursive stack O(log n)

realWorld: Priority queues in Dijkstra, Prim, and other algorithms
Real-time scheduling — always access highest priority task
whenToUse: Need O(log n) insert and O(log n) extract-max
K largest/smallest elements from a stream
alternatives: Sorted array — O(n log n) build, O(1) max, O(n) insert
BST — O(log n) all ops but more complex
Fibonacci heap — better amortized for Dijkstra
